=== page
Primary Corporate Operating Risk: Operational Risk
How will this investment manage or mitigate the Primary Corporate Operating Risk?
Approving this funding ensures that The City’s technology foundation remains consistent, resilient, and secure. Additionally,
it supports growth and is future-focused allowing business units to develop and support technology for their critical
infrastructure relied upon by residents and businesses.
Risk(s) of Not Proceeding (Approving) This Capital Spending Request
Calgary City Net is The City's digital artery, connecting nearly every operational technology environment, including the
Emergency Operations Centre, fire halls, 911-related environments, Transit operations and corporate security systems. This
infrastructure is not optional. Essential services depend on it, including those with direct health, life and safety implications.
Impacts extend beyond IT. Disruptions would be felt directly by Calgarians. Key risks include:
• Greater risk that Calgarians experience delays or disruptions in services that rely on City Net, including emergency
response, public safety, Transit operations and frontline service delivery.
• Less reliable access to tools Calgarians use in urgent or everyday situations, including public help phones, such as
the Transit Help Phones, and next-train arrival signs.
• More unplanned equipment failures, which can lead to sudden service disruptions for Calgarians, longer recovery
times when failures occur, and higher costs than planned lifecycle renewal.
If City Net becomes less reliable, the services that depend on it become less reliable.
Risk(s) of Proceeding (Approving) This Capital Spending Request
The recommended funding level and cash flow timing will result in a delay in key lifecycle replacement activities. This will
increase operating costs through extended vendor support and maintenance requirements. Reduced investment will delay
dependent projects by up to 6 months, with some initiatives potentially unable to proceed. This will create disparities in
service delivery across City facilities and increase the risk of service degradation and disruption as aging infrastructure
remains in service beyond its supported lifecycle.

and elevator help phones, and emergency communications, while reducing dependency on third‑party vendors and public
internet availability. They enable faster incident response and recovery, preserve compatibility with legacy and safety‑critical
systems, and strengthen governance, accountability, and resilience across municipal operations.
Risk(s) of Not Proceeding (Approving) This Capital Spending Request
Delaying investment increases outage risk, avoidable operating costs, safety concerns, contact centre impacts, obsolete
collaboration spaces, and security issues from unmanaged mobile devices.
Risk(s) of Proceeding (Approving) This Capital Spending Request
The reduction of required funding introduces risks to critical communication infrastructure, including the lifecycle and
reliability of wireless tower infrastructure, call centre services, collaboration spaces, and mobile device security. Reduced
investment may require call centre lifecycle and improvement work to be deferred until 2028, increasing the risk of service
disruptions and delaying improvements to reliability and restoration of normal service levels for key contact centres,
including 311 and Transit Access. Continued investment is important to sustaining resilient wireless communications

338 Prairie Economic Gateway – 114 Avenue SE Grade Separation at
Canadian Pacific Kansas City (CPKC)
Department Business Unit
Infrastructure Services Public Spaces Delivery
Investment Description:
Delivered directly by the City as part of the Prairie Economic Gateway: This rail crossing establishes a connection between
Stoney Trail and Prairie Economic Gateway to enable goods movement and travel between Prairie Economic Gateway and
the provincial highway network, including linkages to the CANAMEX corridor and the Calgary International Airport. The
investment leverages prior investments by the province at the 114 Avenue/Stoney Trail interchange by utilizing latent
capacity that was established when that interchange was constructed. The investment also diverts trucks and heavy vehicles
away from historic 114 Avenue SE, which runs directly along the south edge of the Hamlet of Shepard community, onto a
new roadway to provide a buffer for existing residences. The grade separation removes conflicts between vehicles and rail,

369 Lifecycle Replacement-Desktop
Department Business Unit
People, Innovation & Collaboration Services Information Technology
Investment Description:
Investment in an IT Asset Management (ITAM) lifecycle program is necessary to proactively manage the growing
operational, financial, and cybersecurity risks associated with aging and rapidly advancing technology. Without sustained
lifecycle funding, critical assets such as laptops, desktops, and multi‑function printers are kept in service beyond their
supported lifespan, increasing exposure to cyber threats, device failures, and service disruption. These assets often store,
process, or transmit sensitive information, making unsupported operating systems, firmware, and printer platforms a
significant security risk. Additionally, predictable lifecycle investment enables alignment with vendor support models,
modern security controls, and evolving business demands, avoiding inefficient reactive spending and emergency
replacements.

ensuring proper safeguards, oversight, and infrastructure are in place to use AI responsibly and securely. Key initiatives
supported by this capital request include:

modernization of building permit intake and translation services for community programs.
• Automation: more than 100 software bots across over 20 business units, supporting services such as water emergency
notifications and the Branching Out Trees program, while streamlining processes like transit maintenance records, expense
reporting, and payment processing.

and pedestrian counting.
